customer_question: What are the pros and cons of having Allion handle the Declaration Fee wire transfer on our behalf, versus our company transferring the funds directly ourselves?
question_variants: Should we delegate the wire transfer to Allion or pay directly?
Why would a customer choose to have Allion handle payment instead of paying themselves?
actual_issue: The customer was deciding whether to handle their own USD wire transfer for the Declaration Fee or pay an additional fee to have Allion execute the transfer on their behalf.
plain_english_explanation: Self-transfer is generally recommended, since it avoids extra cost and delay. Customers who choose to delegate to Allion typically do so because they want combined/consolidated invoicing across multiple fees, or because their internal accounting department cannot quickly execute a USD-denominated wire transfer. Delegating to Allion costs an additional ¥100,000 and takes approximately 3 weeks to complete.
consultant_answer: We generally recommend self-transfer, since it's faster and avoids the extra fee. Customers who delegate to us usually do so for combined invoicing convenience or because their accounting team can't quickly process a USD wire transfer. Our delegated transfer service costs an additional ¥100,000 and takes about 3 weeks.
decision_logic: Payment method choice should weigh the customer's internal USD wire transfer capability and invoicing-consolidation needs against the added cost and 3-week turnaround of delegating to Allion.
final_recommendation: Default to recommending self-transfer for cost and speed, but offer the Allion-delegated option proactively for customers with USD wire transfer constraints or who want consolidated invoicing.
risk_if_done_wrong: Recommending delegation by default could unnecessarily add ¥100,000 cost and 3 weeks of delay for customers who could easily self-transfer.
